stageMeta.title: Workflow Agent
headerComment: # Stage 09 — Workflow Agent
# L9 = L8 + long-task runtime closure.  Every plugin from Stage 06 is still
# here — sandbox, approval, FS, shell, search, persistence, resume — plus
# the L7 stateful-task closure (todo / plan-mode / goal / workspace over the
# storage stack), the L8 multi-agent closure (subagent registry + spawn/fork
# providers + jobs + job tools), and the L9 workflow closure:
#   dsh-workflow                      workflow seam (abstract — see below)
#   dsh-workflow-worker-thread        the concrete engine: executes a
#                                     model-written orchestration script in
#                                     a fresh worker thread
#   dsh-tool-ralph                    `ralph` tool: fresh-agent loop over the
#                                     workflow + subagent seams (one fresh
#                                     structured-output child per round)
#   dsh-token-meter                   ctx.tokenMeter: per-session token
#                                     accounting folded from the event log
#   dsh-compaction                    compaction seam (abstract — see below)
#   dsh-compaction-basic              token-meter-driven compaction engine:
#                                     auto-compacts when pressure crosses
#                                     thresholdRatio of the context window
#   dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner deterministic oversized tool-result
#                                     pruning (head + marker + tail)
# The architectural step: conversation → task runtime.  Up to L8 the session
# is a conversation that grows unboundedly; L9 makes long multi-round tasks
# sustainable — tokenMeter measures context pressure, compaction-basic folds
# old surface events into a summary node, the pruner bounds oversized tool
# results, and ralph runs a bounded fresh-agent loop over a real workflow
# engine.
# Seam pattern note (not gaps): dsh-jobs, dsh-compaction and dsh-workflow
# are abstract Service Definitions.  Each is listed (disabled) so the
# closure stays visible in inspect/diff, while exactly one concrete
# implementation carries the runtime — dsh-jobs-local, dsh-compaction-basic
# and dsh-workflow-worker-thread respectively.  Mounting the abstract entry
# alongside its implementation fails loudly: dsh-jobs' constructor rejects
# direct mounting by design; the other two would duplicate-register their
# service name.
# One inherited entry deviates from its Stage 06 source:
#   - dsh-tool-fs-search carries a config block here.  The rc.6 schema made
#     `sampleOverCapGlobResults` a required key; Stage 06's yml predates
#     that requirement and cannot be modified from this stage.
# The persona is frozen (byte-for-byte identical to L4/L5/L6) so the whole
# L4→L9 progression remains a single-variable experiment.
# Second L9 closure — workflow tool + code runtime:
#   dsh-tool-workflow    model-written JS orchestration over ctx.workflowEngine
#   dsh-code-runtime     DISABLED (abstract seam; worker-thread provides it)
#   dsh-code-runtime-worker-thread  code-execution backend (containment, not
#                        security); consumer is dsh-tools Code Mode, gated by
#                        its mode config (default native — tool face unchanged)
stageMeta.driverQuestion: Build a tiny CLI in this workspace. First record a todo list with one task per step. Then: create hello.py that prints "hello"; run it; add a --name flag that greets a named person; run it again; add a --count flag that repeats the greeting N times; run it once more. Finally summarize what you built and how you verified each step.

entry.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode
entry.configYaml:
config:
    # Required non-empty string: the deployment-owned guidance section shown
    # in each model request while plan mode is active.
    section: Plan mode is active. Do not make changes yet — explore, then present a complete plan via exit_plan_mode.

entry.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-goal
entry.configYaml:
config:
    # Schema default made explicit: a goal may drive at most this many
    # autonomous continuation rounds before it must complete or block.
    defaultMaxGoalRounds: 256

entry.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal
entry.configYaml:
config:
    # Schema default made explicit: after this many consecutive autonomous
    # rounds without progress the goal is marked blocked instead of looping.
    blockedAfterConsecutiveRounds: 3
# dsh-workspace injects ["storageDomain", "sessionPersistence"].  The latter
# comes from dsh-session-persistence-jsonl above; the former is provided by
# the three-layer storage stack mounted here (hub → backend → form), listed
# in data-dependency order:

entry.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-sqlite
entry.configYaml:
config:
    # Required: database file path.  Parent directories are created by the
    # backend itself (mkdir recursive in openDatabase), so nesting under the
    # stage's sessions root is safe in the disposable temp workspace.
    path: ./sessions/workspace.db
    # journalMode defaults to "wal".

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread
comments: # No config: inject ["subagents"] is satisfied; defaults — provider
# the engine that gives ctx.workflowEngine a real start(): scripts run in

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ralph
entries.configYaml:
config:
    # Must name a FRESH provider (inheritsParentContext = false) with
    # structured-output support — "spawn" qualifies, "fork" is rejected
    # by requireFreshProvider at execution time.
    subagentProvider: spawn
    # Deployment ceiling for ralph rounds (schema default 256); one fresh
    # child agent is started per round, carrying only the immutable
    # objective plus the previous bounded handoff.
    maxRounds: 256
  # inject ["tools", "workflowEngine", "subagents", "systemPrompt"] is now
  # fully satisfied — ralph is live, not a hollow seam.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter
comments: # No config — the schema is empty and rejects every key ("no settings
# are supported").  The meter folds token usage from the session log and
# answers context-pressure queries for the compaction engine.
# DISABLED — abstract seam: dsh-compaction is the Service Definition for
# ctx.compaction.  Unlike dsh-jobs its constructor does not guard, but
# mounting it alongside dsh-compaction-basic fails with duplicate service
# "compaction" — exactly one implementation per context.  Listed for
# closure visibility; the engine below carries the runtime.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic
entries.configYaml:
config:
    # All values below are the schema defaults, made explicit for reading.
    # Compact when measured pressure reaches 80% of the routed model's
    # contextWindow (see dsh-llm-pi-ai above: 1,000,000 tokens)...
    thresholdRatio: 0.8
    # ...and keep the most recent ~16% of the window verbatim; everything
    # older is folded into one summary node.
    retainRatio: 0.16
    # auto = between-step pressure checks + request-overflow recovery.
    # summarizationProvider/summarizationModel stay unset (empty pair =
    # reuse the compacted agent's own routed provider/model).
    auto: true

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner
comments: # No config: deterministic pruning defaults — tool results over
# thresholdChars 8192 are replaced by head 4096 + marker + tail 1024.
